item.title: Firefly Viewing in Nara: Summer Evenings by the Water — Guide
item.description: For a few weeks in early summer, usually late May into June, Nara offers one of Japan’s most magical fleeting sights: the soft glow of fireflies (hotaru) drifting over its ponds and waterways after dark. The gentle streams and clean water around the old capital — from the reflective Sarusawa Pond with its Ukimido pavilion to Isuien’s garden channels and the quiet moats and rivers on the city’s fringes — provide the still, unpolluted habitat these luminous insects need.

item.title: Inuyama Cormorant Fishing: Firelit Nights on the Kiso River — Guide
item.description: Ukai, the ancient art of fishing with trained cormorants, has been practised on the Kiso River for some 1,300 years, and Inuyama’s summer performances unfold in one of its finest settings — the dark river beneath the floodlit silhouette of Japan’s oldest castle keep. From June to mid-October, spectators board wooden yakata boats hung with lanterns and drift alongside the fishing craft as usho masters in traditional grass skirts and ceremonial dress work a dozen leashed birds by the light of blazing pine-fire baskets, the flames, splashing and handlers' calls conjuring a scene unchanged for centuries.
